title: Amazon rainforest dieback threshold
bottleneck: The Amazon may be approaching a tipping point where deforestation and warming flip it from rainforest to savanna, but the threshold is deeply uncertain: the Global Tipping Points report revised the danger zone down toward 1.5 C of warming combined with current deforestation rates, yet models disagree on whether dieback would be gradual or abrupt, regional or basin-wide. Moisture-recycling feedbacks that sustain the forest are weakening in ways satellites are only beginning to track.
why_it_blocks: The Amazon stores ~100 billion tonnes of carbon and drives rainfall across South America; dieback would release massive emissions and collapse agriculture downwind. Uncertainty about the threshold paralyzes policy — no one can say how close the edge is.
current_state: A Nature Sustainability study warned over a fifth of ecosystems could face catastrophic breakdown within a human lifetime, with the Amazon iconic among them. Monitoring of flying rivers and forest resilience is improving, but early-warning indicators for the tipping point itself remain contested.
